results.description:
"Russia can technologically help the US build an LNG plant in Alaska...the Polar LNG project worth $25 billion"

"What does Russia need from the US in the Arctic? "two things...first is the market, second is iron. The lifting of sanctions on the Arctic LNG-2 and its LNG carriers will bring back buyers from Japan, India, Southeast Asia and remove the discount that is now being taken away by the only client - China"

"A diesel deal with the United States, an opportunity to expand the supply of Russian fertilizers, and now Russia is offering to work together in the Arctic. How could the Arctic unite Russia and the United States, and what can Moscow offer Washington in return for lifting sanctions on Russian gas?

Russia is working on the possibility of joint work with the United States in the Arctic, Russian President Vladimir Putin said.

"In the Arctic, which I mentioned, we are actively working with many countries of the world and are interested in working together. Quite recently, European partners worked with us in our fields. Now we are working on the possibility of joint work with American partners," Putin said at the summit of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF).

What kind of joint work with the United States can Russia have?

We are talking about LNG projects. Indeed, after 2022, due to sanctions against Russia, European companies withdrew from participating in gas projects with Russia - in Yamal LNG and Arctic LNG-2. However, cooperation with Chinese companies has reached a new level, says Igor Yushkov, an expert at the National Energy Security Fund (NEF) and the Financial University under the Government of the Russian Federation. There are two Chinese shareholders in the Arctic LNG 2 - CNPC and CNOOC, which were initially afraid of US sanctions against the project and froze their participation. However, Beijing did not change its policy, just the Chinese companies CNPC and CNOOC did not risk access to the dollar, says Mikhail Vakilyan, an expert at the Institute for the Development of Fuel and Energy Technologies.

But after a year and a half, everything changed. In the second half of 2025, China began buying gas from the sanctioned Arctic LNG-2 plant, allocating an entire terminal for the project, and this year opened a second terminal only for Russian LNG. China has even resumed the delivery of modules for the completion of the third stage of the Arctic LNG-2, although earlier deliveries were suspended.

What does Russia need from the United States in the Arctic? "Russia needs two things. The first is the market, the second is iron. The lifting of sanctions on the Arctic LNG-2 and its LNG carriers will bring back buyers from Japan, India, Southeast Asia and remove the discount that is now being taken away by the only client - China. As for iron, the liquefaction compressors at Yamal LNG and Arctic LNG-2 drive the turbines of Baker Hughes, and this is an American company. Service, spare parts and modernization of these cars run into American export bans," says Vakilyan.

"Here is the same scheme as with the diesel deal. We offer the United States mutually beneficial projects and cooperation in the economy in general in exchange for easing anti-Russian sanctions and putting pressure on Ukraine. We show that this cooperation can be very multifaceted and in different areas: diesel, fertilizers, LNG, and so on,"

- says the expert of the National Energy Security Fund and the Financial University under the Government of the Russian Federation.

What can Russia offer the United States in the field of LNG in exchange for the lifting of sanctions? Russia can technologically help the United States build an LNG plant in Alaska. We are talking about the Polar LNG project worth $25 billion.

"Novatek has a technological solution for the LNG project in Alaska, which it applied to the Arctic LNG 2. These are reinforced concrete platforms on which liquefaction equipment is poured - and this is, in fact, an LNG plant. Novatek has already built two such platforms with equipment, and has built a center for the construction of large-capacity offshore structures in Belokamenka. The problem is that both this center and the Arctic LNG-2 plant itself fell under US sanctions. Therefore, we can build such a plant in Alaska in exchange for the lifting of sanctions at least from the center for the construction of large-capacity platforms," Yushkov says.

According to him, Russia can pour a platform in this center, build the LNG plant itself on it and only then drive it to Alaska. This is a simpler solution, because it is expensive to build something in the Arctic itself, and creates restrictions on time and the possibility of importing equipment, etc.

"It is not a fact that this story will come to fruition, because there are many sanctions problems and questions about the economics of the project, but nevertheless, the Americans are interested in our technologies for Alaska, and Russia uses and says that it can do it,"

- says Yushkov. However, we should not forget that Russia is the main competitor of the United States in terms of gas, and in recent years, the American leadership has consistently squeezed Russian gas out of the European market, the expert adds. And helping LNG from the United States to occupy the market share that the Russian Federation has lost is not a good idea.

However, in addition to the Arctic LNG 2, there is another Russian project that could benefit from cooperation with the United States. This is Yamal LNG, which is not affected by US sanctions. However, the problem is different. From January 1, 2027, the EU bans the supply of any Russian LNG. "In the first half of the year, Europe took almost all of the plant's products - 9.89 million tons. In two months, these volumes need a new route and a new buyer – and an American trader looks natural in this place," says Vakilyan."

-Vzglyad

results.title: Chinese/Russian deals centered on oil-for-loan financing: China lent tens of billions repaid via discounted crude shipments (often no cash),
results.description:
Chinese/Russian deals centered on oil-for-loan financing: China lent tens of billions repaid via discounted crude shipments (often no cash), with CNPC/Sinopec JVs in underdeveloped fields. Russia used similar loans and Rosneft/Roszarubezhneft stakes for oil prepayments. Goals: secure cheap energy supplies and geopolitical footholds amid sanctions. Venezuela gained credit access but received limited investment, low production gains, and reduced revenue.

The US deal grants NABEP (US-backed, 35% gov stake) 100-year concessions on 17 fields (~65B barrels, some prior Chinese/Russian ops). Goals: displace rivals, secure crisis reserves/SPR access (20% at cost + first refusal), revive output via up to $100B investment. Venezuela gets royalties/taxes (~$19/bbl, $200B+ projected), jobs, and market-oriented production growth—but faces long-term lock-in and legitimacy questions from opposition.

results.title: Russia and China call themselves close partners.
results.description:
Russia and China call themselves close partners. But look at their trade, and one country holds the stronger hand. 🇨🇳🇷🇺

Since the invasion of Ukraine, Russian oil and gas have moved east, while Chinese machinery and electronics flow into Russia.Beijing gains a major energy supplier. Moscow gains a customer and goods it cannot easily replace.
China supplies roughly 40 % of Russia's imports. Russia accounts for only about 4 % of China's global trade.

results.title: 🔴 Russia's Indonesia oil stake offers no shield against China claims Russian state oil company Zarubezhneft holds 50% of the Tuna gas block
results.description:
🔴 Russia's Indonesia oil stake offers no shield against China claims

Russian state oil company Zarubezhneft holds 50% of the Tuna gas block in Indonesia's exclusive economic zone off the Natuna Islands—waters China claims under its nine-dash line. In 2021, when a rig arrived to drill, a Chinese coast guard vessel appeared within days and demanded Indonesia halt work in what Beijing called Chinese territory. Indonesia refused and completed exploration.
Zarubezhneft's ownership provided no protection then and offers none now.
